A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EVOLvE/BanditBench study. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original LLM bandit experiments, including win-rates in Tables 1–2, ablations and empirical regret analyses in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and reports additional results on action-space size, generalization and exploration behavior in Tables 3–5 and A4–A5.

M1.justification: The UCB/LinUCB guidance, oracle trajectory generation, few-shot procedure and fine-tuning objective remain unchanged. The added comparison with behavior cloning explains the existing approach without introducing a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 16 Bernoulli/Gaussian MAB configurations and two MovieLens contextual-bandit configurations. Table 4 isolates easy-to-hard transfer within training and evaluation configurations already covered in v1. The newly named Core/HardCore subsets are recommendations, not additional evaluated domains.

E2.justification: The evaluated models, RH/SH comparisons and UCB/LinUCB references remain unchanged, including the full appendix model lists. GPT and Claude names added in Table A3 concern estimated API costs, not new exploration-performance baselines.

E3.justification: v2 adds MinFrac and OptFrac evaluation at steps 100, 250, 500, 750 and 1000, averaged across Bernoulli configurations. This supplements the existing evaluation protocol; the main settings, win-rate calculation and documented training configurations remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands behavioral analysis: Table 3 examines when AG helps across action-space sizes, Table 4 isolates easy-to-hard transfer, and Tables 5/A4/A5 examine exploration allocation and optimal-arm selection over time. The earlier representation ablations and regret-fitting analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify 30 independent trials, seeds 0–29 and Student’s t-tests with p < 0.05 for win-rates. The added analyses do not introduce new run counts, confidence intervals or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: The headline results in Tables 1–2 and appendix model lists remain unchanged, but v2 adds substantial numerical evidence. Table 4 reports hard-task win-rates of 34.0% for Flash (SH), 43.0% for few-shot (SH) and 48.4% for OFT (RH) using easy-task demonstrations. Tables 3, 5 and A3–A5 add disaggregated performance, behavioral trajectories and cost estimates.

T1.justification: The regret and sufficient-textualization definitions, UCB/LinUCB mathematics, fine-tuning loss and regret-fitting function are retained. The behavior-cloning discussion is conceptual explanation, while MinFrac and OptFrac supplement empirical evaluation without adding a formal theoretical result.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statement and conclusion retain the same central claims: BanditBench, algorithm-guided support and distillation, smaller models outperforming larger ones, and a remaining gap to classical algorithms. The added evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 replaces the broad claim that support improves all models with emphasis on larger models and complex environments. It adds interpretations distinguishing OFT from behavior cloning and uses exploration diagnostics to argue that Flash shows limited adaptation and directed exploration. These substantially expand the account of mechanisms and failure conditions.

D1.justification: v2 adds repository and package-installation instructions, a Software and Data section, and inference-cost assumptions and estimates in Appendix A.5. Experiment-log release is promised rather than established. Existing prompts, trajectory counts, seeds and sampling temperature remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 broadens its positioning through an explicit behavior-cloning comparison, additional LLM bandit research and a new connection to human directed/random exploration. It adds references including Pomerleau, Felicioni, Rahn, Wilson, Daw and Gershman, while removing the LLM-as-optimizer discussion and Yang citation.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and much of the prose remain intact. v2 revises results discussion and headings, expands explanations, adds Software and Data and acknowledgements sections, and renumbers appendix sections. Related-work editing also introduces some repeated discussion.

P2.justification: v2 adds six tables: Tables 3–5 and A3–A5. Figure 4 changes from compact heatmaps to two full-width line-chart panels displaying the same results, with an expanded caption. Other figures receive limited labeling or placement changes, while the appendix prompt displays are retained.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1’s aggregate comparisons, v2 provides useful evidence about action-space effects, transfer and exploration behavior, alongside clearer software-access and cost information. These improve scrutiny and reuse, but the gain is limited: MinFrac normalization is unexplained despite reported values such as 82.3%, weakening the new behavioral interpretation, and related-work prose is partly duplicated. The original method and headline evidence remain unchanged.
